demand_drivers.body:
- Expanding domestic market driven by a growing middle-income group and rising consumption trends.
- Rising global demand from supply-chain shifts due to geopolitical factors favours India.
- Government support (PLI Scheme, RoSCTL, export incentives for garments and made-ups) aids the textile industry.
- India's Free Trade Agreements with Australia, UK, Oman and New Zealand, with negotiations ongoing with the US, EU, Canada and SACU countries, are expected to raise export opportunities.
- The Union Budget 2026-27 prioritises the textile sector for job creation and export growth; the textile sector is …

capex_expansion.body: The company proposes to take up the next phase of its Rental Services segment during the current year, developing about 1,20,000 sq. ft of space to be completed by 2027-28; its Bankers have agreed to fund the project. In the ensuing financial year 2026-27, the company's 8.5 MW Solar power is expected to operate at full capacity.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body: distribution: The company's mall is situated in the heart of the city with tenants of good brands attracting large consumers — evidence: rental income rose on account of revenue sharing, events conducted and new tenants during the year.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Company-flagged exposure on inventory valuation, EBITDA, finished-goods pile-up, power cost and unhedged forex.
- Company-flagged exposure to working-capital blockage, timely term-loan permits and statutory dues.
- Company-flagged exposure to technology upgradation needs, labour shortage and quality claims.
- SEBI LODR obligations including quarterly results, Related Party omnibus approvals and board composition requirements.
- Compliance with Pollution Control Board norms, labour laws, the Code on Wages, PF and ESI.
- Countries like Bangladesh and Vietnam offer lower production costs and benefit from preferential trade agreements, challenging market share of traditional leaders like India.
- New or impending punitive tariffs, particularly from major markets like the US, can decrease profit margins and reduce export competitiveness.
- Erratic yields due to climate change lead to high volatility in natural fibre prices (e.g. cotton), squeezing margins for manufacturers with low pricing power.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- In spinning, the company is moving towards a wider fibre mix, more specialised yarn and sustainability, blending four fibers in one yarn.
- Focus is steadily shifting towards application-based yarns that offer a functional and commercial edge rather than commodity yarn.
- The raw material basket is diversifying within cotton (organic, BCI, recycled cotton fibre) and into linen, hemp, bamboo, tencel and silk.
- Proposed next phase of Rental Services expansion of about 1,20,000 sq. ft, bank-funded, to be completed by 2027-28.
